Introduction

The Philippines is home to some of the most stunning natural wonders in Southeast Asia. From limestone lagoons and island chains to roaring waterfalls and sea-of-clouds summits, here are five spots every traveler should see.

Luzon

Mt. Pulag

Straddling Benguet, Ifugao, and Nueva Vizcaya, Mt. Pulag is the highest peak in Luzon at about 2,922 meters above sea level. Hikers start before sunrise to reach the grassy summit in time for the famous sea of clouds, and the Ambangeg trail is the easiest route for beginners.

Luzon

Hundred Islands, Pangasinan

Found in Alaminos City, this national park is made up of more than a hundred small limestone islands scattered across Lingayen Gulf. Popular stops include Quezon Island for swimming, Governor's Island for its viewing deck, and Children's Island for its shallow, calm beach. It is an easy trip from Manila.

Luzon

Taal Volcano, Batangas

Taal is one of the smallest active volcanoes in the world, set on an island inside a lake that fills an ancient caldera. The classic view is from the ridge at Tagaytay, about two hours from Manila. Access to the island depends on volcano alert levels set by PHIVOLCS, so check the latest advisory before planning a visit.

Palawan

El Nido, Palawan

El Nido sits on the northern tip of Palawan and is known for the towering limestone cliffs of Bacuit Bay. Visitors take island hopping tours to hidden lagoons, white sand beaches, and snorkeling spots, and kayaking through the calm, clear water is a favorite way to explore.

Visayas

Kawasan Falls, Cebu

Kawasan Falls is in Badian, in southwestern Cebu, and is famous for its bright turquoise pools. Swimmers can cool off at the base of the falls, while adventurous visitors join canyoneering tours that include cliff jumps and river walks upstream.
